definitions.explanation: Thread or yarn spun from cotton fibers. Used in textile manufacturing, sewing, and crafts.

examples.japanese: この{布|ぬの}は{綿糸|めんし}で{織|お}られている。
examples.english: This cloth is woven with cotton yarn.

examples.japanese: {綿糸|めんし}は{肌|はだ}に{優|やさ}しいので{赤|あか}ちゃんの{服|ふく}によく{使|つか}われる。
examples.english: Cotton yarn is gentle on the skin, so it is often used for baby clothes.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}、{日本|にほん}の{綿糸|めんし}{生産|せいさん}は{急速|きゅうそく}に{発展|はってん}し、{主要|しゅよう}な{輸出品|ゆしゅつひん}の{一|ひと}つとなった。
examples.english: During the Meiji era, Japan's cotton yarn production developed rapidly and became one of the major exports.

notes:
Combines {綿|めん} (cotton) and {糸|し} (thread, yarn). An important term in Japanese economic history, as cotton spinning was one of the first modern industries in Meiji-era Japan. Today used in textile and craft contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {綿糸|めんし}{紡績|ぼうせき}: cotton spinning
- {綿糸|めんし}で{編|あ}む: to knit with cotton yarn
- {綿糸|めんし}の{生産|せいさん}: cotton yarn production
- {太|ふと}{番手|ばんて}の{綿糸|めんし}: thick-count cotton yarn

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {絹糸|けんし}: silk thread — a more luxurious fiber
- {毛糸|けいと}: wool yarn — used for knitting, read with kun'yomi
- {木綿|もめん}: cotton (fabric) — the finished textile rather than the yarn
